items.prompt: Sam wants to use the foods that are still good. Put them in order. Use the soonest date first.
items.hint: Leave out the foods whose dates have passed. Then find the date closest to October 14.
items.explain: Eggs come first (October 18), then yogurt (October 20), then cheese (October 30). The dates are in the Best before column.

items.prompt: Priya's dad gets a flat tire on the way. They get to the observatory at 7:45 PM. What should Priya do?
options: Sit in Row C, Seat 8 right away.
Wait at the back until 8:15 PM.
Go home. The show is over.
items.hint: Is 7:45 PM before or after the show starts? Then read the last row.
items.explain: Priya should wait at the back until 8:15 PM. The show starts at 7:30 PM, so 7:45 PM is late, and the Late? row says to wait until the break.

items.prompt: Priya finds the seats. Tap her seat.
items.hint: Find the Seat row on the ticket. Check the row letter first, then the seat number.
items.explain: Priya sits in Row C, Seat 8. It is in the Seat row of her ticket.

items.prompt: Ana cannot eat nuts. What should she do with the banana bread?
options: Skip it. The label says it may contain nuts.
Eat a slice. Nuts are missing from the Contains row.
items.hint: Read every row about what is in the bread. There are two of them.
items.explain: Ana should skip it. The May contain row says nuts, so the bread might have nuts in it.

items.prompt: Grandma Rose gives each soccer player one serving. Tap the row that tells how many players one loaf can feed.
items.hint: First find how big one serving is. Then find how many of those are in a loaf.
items.explain: Tap the Slices in a loaf row. It says 8. One serving is 1 slice, so one loaf feeds 8 players.

items.prompt: Ben needs 8 juice boxes for the team. How much will he pay?
items.hint: Read the whole juice box row. It has two prices. Pick the one that matches 8 boxes.
items.explain: Ben pays $6. The juice box row says 8 for $6. That costs less than 8 boxes at $1 each, which would be $8.

items.prompt: Ben takes 3 pretzel packs. How much will he pay?
items.hint: Read the deal in the pretzel row. Work out how many packs he pays for.
items.explain: Ben pays $4. Pretzel packs are $2 each, and when you buy 2 you get 1 more free. He pays for 2 packs, and $2 + $2 = $4.

items.prompt: Priya eats 2 cups of Rocket Oats. How many grams of added sugars does she eat?
items.hint: Read the note to find how big one serving is. Then find the Added sugars amount and count how many servings she eats.
items.explain: She eats 20 g. The note says 1 serving is 1 cup, and the Added sugars row says 10 g in 1 serving. 2 cups is 2 servings, so 10 g + 10 g = 20 g.

items.prompt: Use the note under the label. Sort each nutrient by its % Daily Value.
items.hint: Find each nutrient's row and read its % Daily Value. Compare it with 5% and with 20%.
items.explain: Total fat (3%) is low. Sodium (8%) and fiber (18%) are in between. Added sugars (20%) and iron (20%) are high, because the note says 20% or more is high.

items.prompt: Ben's mom reads the label with him. Ben is 12. He has a dose at 8:00 AM. What is the earliest time the label allows his next dose? Ask an adult before you take any medicine.
items.hint: Find the row that says how often. Add that many hours to 8:00 AM.
items.explain: The earliest next dose is at 2:00 PM. The How often row says every 6 hours, and 6 hours after 8:00 AM is 2:00 PM. Ask an adult before you take any medicine.

items.prompt: Ben's mom reads the label with him. Ben is 12. How much is one dose for him, and what should it be measured with? Ask an adult before you take any medicine.
options: 15 mL, with the cup in the box
10 mL, with the cup in the box
items.hint: Find the row with Ben's age. Then find the row that says how to measure.
items.explain: One dose is 15 mL, measured with the cup in the box. The Ages 12 and up row says 15 mL, and the Measure with row says to use the cup in this box only. Ask an adult before you take any medicine.

items.prompt: Sort each plan. Does Leo's ticket allow it?

cards.text: Leave for lunch and come back in once
Leave and come back in a second time
Sign up for the tournament at 10:30 AM
Sign up for the tournament at 11:30 AM

items.hint: Read the Bags, Re-entry and Game tournament rows. Check each plan against the rule in its row.
items.explain: A small backpack, leaving once and signing up at 10:30 AM are allowed. A large bag, coming back in a second time and signing up at 11:30 AM are not. The rules are in the Bags, Re-entry and Game tournament rows.

items.prompt: Leo's little brother is 8. He wants to come to the fair too. Which plan follows the ticket rules?
options: He goes in on his own.
He goes in with Leo, who is 13.
He goes in with Leo's dad, and they both have tickets.
He goes in with Leo's dad, who waits outside the gate.
items.hint: Find the row about children under 10. Check who he must stay with, and what that person needs.
items.explain: He goes in with Leo's dad, and they both have tickets. The Under age 10 row says he must stay with an adult who has a ticket. Leo is 13, so he is not an adult.

items.prompt: Maya's dad reads the label with her. Maya takes her first dose on the morning of March 3. On what day does she take her last dose? Ask an adult before you take any medicine.
items.hint: Find how many days she takes it. Count the days, with March 3 as day 1.
items.explain: Her last dose is on March 12. The How long row says 10 days. If March 3 is day 1, then day 10 is March 12. Ask an adult before you take any medicine.

items.prompt: Maya's dad reads the label with her. Maya forgot her morning dose. She remembers at 6:00 PM. Her night dose is at 8:00 PM. What does the label say to do? Ask an adult before you take any medicine.
options: Take the missed dose now. Then take the night dose at 8:00 PM.
Skip the missed dose. Take the night dose at 8:00 PM as usual.
Skip both doses today. Start again tomorrow morning.
items.hint: Find the row about a missed dose. Work out how many hours it is until her next dose.
items.explain: She skips the missed dose and takes the night dose at 8:00 PM. The Missed a dose? row says to skip it if the next dose is less than 4 hours away, and 8:00 PM is only 2 hours after 6:00 PM. Ask an adult before you take any medicine.

items.prompt: Ana cannot eat peanuts or tree nuts. Which bar is safe for her, and how much does one of those bars cost?
items.hint: Check both the Contains row and the May contain row for every bar. Then share the box price over the bars in the box.
items.explain: Rocket Rice is safe, and one bar costs 50 cents. Trail Blaze contains peanuts, and Summit Crunch may contain peanuts. Rocket Rice is $4 for 8 bars, so each bar is 50 cents.

items.prompt: The coach buys the bar that is safe for Ana. There are 16 players, and each player gets one bar. Bars come only in full boxes. How much does the coach pay?
items.hint: First find the bar that is safe for Ana. Then work out how many of its boxes make 16 bars.
items.explain: The coach pays $8. Rocket Rice is the only bar with no peanuts or tree nuts. A box of Rocket Rice has 8 bars for $4, so 16 bars is 2 boxes, and 2 boxes cost $8.

items.prompt: How much food does Pixel need each day?
items.hint: Find Pixel's weight first. Then find the row whose weights include it.
items.explain: Pixel needs 2 cups a day. He weighs 25 pounds, and the Dogs 21 to 40 pounds row says 2 cups a day.

items.prompt: Sam splits Pixel's food into meals, like the bag says. How much food goes in each meal?
items.hint: Find how much food Pixel gets in a day. Then read the Meals row and share the food out.
items.explain: Each meal is 1 cup. Pixel gets 2 cups a day, and the Meals row says to split it into 2 meals.

items.prompt: Maya plants the seeds on May 3. What is the earliest day she might see sprouts?
items.hint: Find the row that says how long sprouts take. Use the smaller number, and count that many days on from May 3.
items.explain: The earliest day is May 10. The Days to sprout row says 7 to 10 days, and 7 days after May 3 is May 10.

items.prompt: Maya digs a hole for one seed. Tap the hole that matches the packet.
items.hint: Two rows have inches in them. Find the one about how deep to plant.
items.explain: Maya digs the hole 1 inch deep. The Planting depth row says 1 inch. The 12 inches row is the space between seeds.

items.prompt: What should Ben wear on the trip?
options: The jacket with a sweater under it
items.hint: The forecast has two parts. Find the row about rain and the row about cold days.
items.explain: Ben should wear the jacket with a sweater under it. The Rain row says it keeps him dry in heavy rain, and the Warmth row says to wear a sweater under it on cold days.

items.prompt: Ben's jacket is muddy after the trip. Sort what he should do when he washes it.
items.hint: Read the Wash row and the Dry row. Check each card against them.
items.explain: Ben washes it in cold water, closes the zips first and hangs it up to dry. He skips hot water and the dryer. The rules are in the Wash and Dry rows.

items.prompt: Leo and Maya each buy a small bucket. How much do they pay, and what do they get for free?
items.hint: Find the small bucket price and count two buckets. Then read the Deal row.
items.explain: They pay $12 and get a free geode. A small bucket is $6, so two cost $6 + $6 = $12. The Deal row says 2 small buckets get 1 geode free.

items.prompt: Sam gets to the mine at 3:45 PM. What can he still buy?
items.hint: Find the two rows that say when things are sold. Compare each time with 3:45 PM.
items.explain: Sam can still buy a geode. The Buckets sold row says buckets stop at 3:30 PM, but the Geodes sold row says geodes are sold until 5 PM.

items.prompt: Priya and her mom get to Harbor Park. Tap the gate Priya should use.
items.hint: Find Priya's section number. Then find the row that says which gate goes with that section.
items.explain: Priya uses the North Gate. Her seat is in Section 3, and the Which gate row says Sections 1 to 4 use the North Gate.

items.prompt: Priya's mom wants to bring her big backpack and an umbrella. The forecast says light rain. What should she bring instead?
options: A clear bag 12 by 12 inches or smaller, and an umbrella
Her big backpack and a rain poncho
A clear bag 12 by 12 inches or smaller, and a rain poncho
A small dark bag and a rain poncho
items.hint: Read the Bags row and the Rain row. The right answer follows both rules.
items.explain: She should bring a clear bag 12 by 12 inches or smaller, and a rain poncho. The Bags row says clear bags only, and the Rain row says no umbrellas in the seats but rain ponchos are fine.

items.prompt: Priya and her mom want to be at the gate when it opens. The drive to Harbor Park takes 25 minutes. What is the latest time they can leave home?
items.hint: Find the row for when the gates open. Count back 25 minutes from that time.
items.explain: They must leave by 5:35 PM. The Gates open row says 6:00 PM, and 25 minutes before 6:00 PM is 5:35 PM.

items.prompt: Sam's cousin will be 6. What does the box say about a child his age?
options: He can dig, but an adult needs to help him.
He is too young. The kit is for ages 8 and up.
He can dig on his own. The warning is only for children under 3.
He can dig on his own if he wears the safety goggles.
items.hint: Read the whole Ages row, not just the first part. Then think about what the warning at the top is about.
items.explain: He can dig, but an adult needs to help him. The Ages row says children under 8 need an adult to help. The warning about children under 3 is about small parts.

items.prompt: Sam wants everything ready before his cousin opens the kit. Sort each thing.
items.hint: Read the In the box row. Then read the You also need row. Check each card against both.
items.explain: The pick, brush, goggles and guide book come in the box. Sam gets the spray bottle of water and old newspaper at home. They are in the You also need row.

items.prompt: What time must Sam check in at Dock 4?
items.hint: Read the warning at the top. Then find when the boat leaves and count back.
items.explain: Sam must check in by 9:30 AM. The Boat leaves row says 10:00 AM, and the warning says to check in 30 minutes before the boat leaves.

items.prompt: On the trip, Sam sees seals and puffins. The boat finds zero whales. What does Sam get?
options: A new date for the same trip
A free ticket for another trip
items.hint: Two rows talk about getting something back. Read both. Pick the one that matches what happened on this trip.
items.explain: Sam gets a free ticket for another trip. The Whale promise row says this happens if the boat sees no whales. The Wind or fog row is for trips that are canceled.

items.prompt: It is 8:15 AM on Sunday. Nobody has called Grandma Rose about the trip. What should they do?
options: Stay home. The trip is canceled.
Wait at home until the company calls.
Pick a new date for the trip.
Go to Dock 4 for the trip. It is going ahead.
items.hint: Read the Wind or fog row. Think about what it means when the call has not come by that time.
items.explain: They should go to Dock 4, because the trip is going ahead. The Wind or fog row says the company calls by 8:00 AM if the trip is canceled. No call came by 8:15 AM.

items.prompt: Priya goes to the shop on May 20. Can she buy the kit and the battery pack with her $40?
options: Yes. The kit costs $36, so she has enough.
No. The kit costs $48, so she cannot buy even the kit.
No. The kit and the pack cost $63 together.
No. The kit costs $36 and the pack costs $15. That is $51.
items.hint: Work out the sale price of the kit first. Then add the battery pack and compare the total with $40.
items.explain: No. On May 20 the sale is on, so the kit costs $48 - $12 = $36. The battery pack costs $15 more, and $36 + $15 = $51. That is more than $40.

items.prompt: Priya puts batteries in the robot and the remote. How many of her AA batteries from home are left?
items.hint: Check which kind of battery each part uses, and which batteries come in the box.
items.explain: She has 2 AA batteries left. The robot uses 4 AA batteries, and 6 - 4 = 2. The remote uses AAA batteries, and those come in the box.

items.prompt: At the robot show, Priya's robot must run for 3 hours without stopping. Which plan works?
options: Use one set of 4 new AA batteries.
Use her 6 AA batteries from home.
Use the battery pack, fully charged.
Use the 2 AAA batteries from the box.
items.hint: Find how long the robot runs on AA batteries and how long it runs on the battery pack. Compare each with 3 hours.
items.explain: Use the battery pack, fully charged. The Battery pack row says it runs the robot for 3 hours. AA batteries last about 90 minutes, and the robot holds only 4 at a time. The AAA batteries are for the remote.

items.prompt: On the map, the trail from the campsite to the old mill is 3 inches long. How far is the walk on the trail?
items.hint: Find the map scale. Work out the trail distance for each inch on the map, then count up to 3 inches.
items.explain: The walk is 1 and a half miles. The Map scale row says 1 inch on the map is half a mile on the trail. Three half miles make 1 and a half miles.

items.prompt: The Diaz family has 5 people. They drive to Story Woods and camp for 2 nights. They use as few tents as they can. How much do they pay to camp and park?
items.hint: Work out how many tents 5 people need. Then find the cost for each tent each night. Last, check the row about cars.
items.explain: They pay $48. Up to 4 people fit in a tent, so 5 people need 2 tents. 2 tents for 2 nights is 4 tent-nights, and 4 x $12 = $48. The car needs no day pass, because they have a camping permit.

items.prompt: Ms. Ortiz gets to the ranger station at 6:30 PM on Friday. She wants to camp that night. Tap the row that shows the problem with her plan.
items.hint: Her plan has a time in it. Look for a row with a time rule, and compare.
items.explain: Tap the Permit hours row. It says to buy a permit by 6:00 PM on the day you arrive, and Ms. Ortiz gets there at 6:30 PM.

items.prompt: What must Leo wear to skate?
items.hint: Find the row that tells what you must wear.
items.explain: Leo must wear a helmet. It is in the You must wear row.

items.prompt: Leo wants to skate until the park closes. What time does it close?
items.hint: Find the row with the park times. The second time tells when it closes.
items.explain: The park closes at 5 PM. The Park open row says 9 AM to 5 PM.

items.prompt: Leo's mom asks if he paid for the pass. Tap the row that tells her.
items.hint: Look for a row with a $ sign.
items.explain: Tap the Price row. It says $3 (paid), so Leo paid.

items.prompt: How many times a day should Maya feed the fish?
items.hint: Find the Feed row. Read the number in it.
items.explain: Maya feeds the fish 2 times a day. It is in the Feed row.

items.prompt: How much food does Maya give the fish each time?
items.hint: Find the How much row. Then read the row under it.
items.explain: Maya gives a small pinch. The How much row says a small pinch, and the next row says too much food makes the water dirty.

items.prompt: There are 5 friends. What does the box say about how many can play at once?
options: Up to 4 can play at once.
items.hint: Find the Players row. Look at the biggest number in it.
items.explain: Up to 4 can play at once. The Players row says 2 to 4, so 5 players is one too many.

items.prompt: They start a game at 4:00 PM. About what time will it end?
items.hint: Find how long one game takes. Add that time to 4:00 PM.
items.explain: The game will end at about 4:30 PM. The Time to play row says about 30 minutes, and 30 minutes after 4:00 PM is 4:30 PM.

items.prompt: Ben wants to check that no boats are missing. Tap the row that tells how many boats should be in the box.
items.hint: Look for the row that lists what comes in the box.
items.explain: Tap the In the box row. It says there are 4 boats.

items.prompt: Priya buys a mask and a snorkel. She does not buy fins. How much does she pay?
items.hint: Find the mask tag and the snorkel tag. Add the two prices.
items.explain: Priya pays $13. The mask is $8 and the snorkel is $5, and $8 + $5 = $13.

items.prompt: Sam wants a mask, a snorkel and fins. Which way costs less?
options: Buy each one alone, for $25 in all.
items.hint: Add the three single prices. Then compare that total with the set price.
items.explain: The set costs less. Alone, the three cost $8 + $5 + $12 = $25. The green sale sign says the set is $20.

items.prompt: Ben comes to the shop on Saturday, the day before the sale ends. Can he still get the set for $20?
options: Yes. The sale is still on.
No. The set is sold only on Sunday.
items.hint: Find the sign that says when the sale ends. Is Saturday before or after that day?
items.explain: Yes. The red sign says the sale ends on Sunday. Ben comes on Saturday, so the sale is still on.

items.prompt: What should Priya do with the seeds the night before she plants them?
items.hint: Find the row that tells what to do before you plant.
items.explain: She should soak the seeds in water overnight. It is in the Before you plant row.

items.prompt: There are 24 students in the class. Each student plants 1 seed. How many seeds are left in the packet?
items.hint: Find how many seeds are in the packet. Take away the seeds the class plants.
items.explain: 6 seeds are left. The Seeds in packet row says 30, and 30 - 24 = 6.

items.prompt: Put the steps from the bean packet in order.
steps: Soak the seeds in water overnight.
Watch for sprouts in 6 to 10 days.
Give each plant a stick to climb.
items.hint: Think about what must happen first. A seed goes in the soil before it can sprout.
items.explain: First soak the seeds overnight. Then plant them 1 inch deep. Then watch for sprouts in 6 to 10 days. Last, give each plant a stick to climb. Each step is in a row of the packet.

items.prompt: On Saturday, Sam rides to the library and then rides home. How many rides are left after that?
items.hint: Find how many rides are on the pass. Count one ride there and one ride back.
items.explain: 3 rides are left. The pass has 5 rides, and going there and back uses 2 rides. 5 - 2 = 3.

items.prompt: Sam wants to use the pass on December 3. What does the pass say?
options: It does not work. It was good until November 30.
It still works, because it has rides left.
items.hint: Find the row with a date. Is December 3 before or after that date?
items.explain: It does not work. The Good until row says November 30, and December 3 is after that.

items.prompt: Ana is 12. She wants a pass like Sam's. Tap the row that tells who can get this pass.
items.hint: Look for a row with ages in it.
items.explain: Tap the Ages row. It says 6 to 17, and Ana is 12, so she can get one.

items.prompt: Maya wants to hear Dr. Bell's talk. Where and when should she go?
items.hint: Find the row with Dr. Bell's name. It has a time and a floor.
items.explain: She should go to Floor 1 at 11 AM. It is in the Dig Pit talk row.

items.prompt: After the talk, Maya wants to see the T. rex skeleton. Tap where she should go.
items.hint: Find the row that names the T. rex. Read which floor it is on.
items.explain: Maya goes to Floor 2, the Dinosaur Hall. The Dinosaur Hall row says the T. rex skeleton is there.

items.prompt: Maya got there at 9:30 AM. What should she do?
options: Go in now. The museum is open.
Wait. The museum opens at 10 AM.
Go home. The museum is closed on Sunday.
items.hint: Find the row that says when the museum is open. Compare 9:30 AM with the first time.
items.explain: Maya should wait. The Museum open row says 10 AM to 4 PM, and 9:30 AM is before 10 AM.

items.prompt: On Saturday, Priya wants to bring Maya to a star show. What does the card say?
options: Neither girl gets in free on Saturday.
Priya gets in free. Maya needs a ticket.
items.hint: Read the Star shows row and the Bring a guest row. Check the day in each one.
items.explain: Priya gets in free, but Maya needs a ticket. The Star shows row says shows are free for members, and the Bring a guest row says a guest is free on Fridays only.

items.prompt: Priya buys a star map poster for $12 at the gift shop. How much does she pay?
items.hint: Read the Gift shop row. Check if $12 is $10 or more.
items.explain: Priya pays $10. The Gift shop row says $2 off anything that costs $10 or more, and $12 - $2 = $10.

items.prompt: Sort each visit. Is it free with Priya's card?

cards.text: Priya at a star show on February 20
Priya at a telescope night on Friday, March 13
Priya at a star show on April 4

items.hint: For each card, check the date against the Good until row. Then check the rule for guests.
items.explain: The star show on February 20, the telescope night on March 13 and a guest on a Friday are free. April 4 is after March 31, when the card ends, and a guest is free on Fridays only.

items.prompt: The school's practice guitars have nylon strings. Can Sam use this pack on them?
options: No. This pack is for steel-string guitars only.
items.hint: Read the whole For row, all the way to the end.
items.explain: No. The For row says these strings are for steel-string guitars only, not for nylon-string guitars.

items.prompt: Sam buys 2 packs. How much does he save, compared with paying the one-pack price for each?
items.hint: Work out the cost of 2 packs at the one-pack price. Then compare it with the deal.
items.explain: Sam saves $2. Two packs at $8 each cost $16. The Price row says 2 packs for $14, and $16 - $14 = $2.

items.prompt: Sam plays every day. He put on all new strings on January 10. About when should he change all of them again?
items.hint: Find the row about changing all the strings. Count that many months on from January 10.
items.explain: About April 10. The Change all strings row says about every 3 months for someone who plays every day, and 3 months after January 10 is April 10.

items.prompt: Maya had the fish tacos and one lemonade. How much does she owe Leo?
items.hint: Find the price of her food. Then find the price of one lemonade, not three.
items.explain: Maya owes $9.00. The fish tacos are $7.00, and the lemonade row says $2.00 each. $7 + $2 = $9.

items.prompt: Leo wants to check how much money Mrs. Lin gave back to him. Tap the row that tells him.
items.hint: Money that comes back to you after you pay has a special name on a receipt. Look near the bottom.
items.explain: Tap the Change row. It says $6.00. Leo paid $30.00, and the total was $24.00.

items.prompt: Ben had the veggie burger and one lemonade. He pays Leo back with a $10 bill. How much change does Leo give Ben?
items.hint: First add up what Ben ate and drank. Then take that away from $10.
items.explain: Leo gives Ben $2.00. The veggie burger is $6.00 and one lemonade is $2.00, so Ben owes $8.00. $10 - $8 = $2.

items.prompt: Priya puts 4 empty AA batteries in the charger at 3:00 PM. About when will they be full?
items.hint: Two rows give charge times. Pick the row for 4 batteries. Then add the hours to 3:00 PM.
items.explain: About 8:00 PM. The Time for 4 AA row says about 5 hours, and 5 hours after 3:00 PM is 8:00 PM. 6:00 PM would be the time for only 2 batteries.

items.prompt: The light on the charger is red. What should Priya do?
items.hint: Find the row for the red light. Then compare it with the row for the green light.
items.explain: Priya should leave the batteries in. The Red light row says they are still charging. She takes them out when the light is green.

items.prompt: Priya finds these batteries in the club box. Sort them.
items.hint: Read the Batteries row for the sizes that fit. Then read the Never charge row.
items.explain: AA and AAA rechargeable batteries can go in. Regular one-use batteries stay out, because the Never charge row says they can leak. The 9-volt stays out too, because the Batteries row lists only AA and AAA.

items.prompt: Which mineral in the set is the hardest?
items.hint: Read the hardness number for each mineral. Find the biggest number.
items.explain: Quartz is the hardest. Its row says hardness 7, the biggest number in the set.

items.prompt: Maya wants to scratch her piece of calcite. Which mineral can scratch it?
items.hint: Read the How it works row. Then find a mineral with a bigger hardness number than calcite.
items.explain: Feldspar can scratch calcite. Feldspar is hardness 6 and calcite is hardness 3, and the How it works row says a harder mineral can scratch a softer one. Talc and gypsum are softer than calcite.

items.prompt: Put these minerals in order, from the softest to the hardest.
items.hint: Find the hardness number for each one. Start with the smallest number.
items.explain: Talc (1), then calcite (3), then feldspar (6), then quartz (7). The numbers are in each mineral's row.

items.prompt: Can Ana wear these cleats for her team's winter games?
options: Yes, if the gym floor is dry.
No. They are not for indoor gym floors.
items.hint: Find where the team plays in winter. Then read the Not for row.
items.explain: No. The team plays in the school gym in winter, and the Not for row says the cleats are not for indoor gym floors.

items.prompt: Ana's cleats are wet and muddy after a game. Which plan follows the tag?
options: Knock off the mud and let them dry in the air.
Put them next to the heater so they dry fast.
Leave the mud on and put them in her bag.
items.hint: Find the Care row. Check each plan against it.
items.explain: Ana should knock off the mud and let them dry in the air. The Care row says this, and it says to keep them away from heaters.

items.prompt: Tap the place where Ana can wear these cleats.
items.hint: Read the Best for row and the Not for row.
items.explain: Ana can wear them on the grass field. The Best for row says firm, dry grass, and the Not for row says gym floors and hard turf.

items.prompt: The forecast says 20°F and light, dry snow. Can Sam wear these gloves?
options: No. They are not for any snow.
No. 20°F is too cold for them.
Yes. The gloves work for both.
items.hint: Check the Warmth row and the Snow row. Compare each one with the forecast.
items.explain: Yes. 20°F is warmer than 10°F, so the gloves keep him warm, and the Snow row says they are good for light, dry snow.

items.prompt: The next morning, it is 30°F with heavy, wet snow. What should Sam wear on his hands?
items.hint: The forecast says wet snow. Find the row about wet snow.
items.explain: Sam should wear waterproof mittens. The Wet snow or rain row says water can get into these gloves.

items.prompt: Sam wants to check the weather app on his phone without taking his gloves off. Tap the row that tells him if he can.
items.hint: Look for a row about phones or screens.
items.explain: Tap the Fingertips row. It says the fingertips work on phone screens, so he can keep his gloves on.

items.prompt: Ben and Leo get to the aquarium at 12:45 PM. What should they do?
options: Go home. They missed their time.
Wait until 1:00 PM, then go in.
items.hint: Find the row that says when to go in. Is 12:45 PM before or inside that time?
items.explain: They should wait until 1:00 PM. The Enter between row says 1:00 PM and 1:30 PM, and 12:45 PM is before that.

items.prompt: Leo wants lunch at 2:00 PM, and he also wants to see the shark feeding. Which plan follows the ticket?
options: Eat at the café inside, then go to the Deep Tank.
Leave for lunch, then come back for the feeding.
Skip lunch, because no food is sold inside.
items.hint: Read the Café row and the Re-entry row. Find the plan that keeps him inside.
items.explain: Leo should eat at the café inside, then go to the Deep Tank. The Re-entry row says he cannot come back in if he leaves, and the Café row says the café is inside and open until 3:00 PM.

items.prompt: Ben's mom paid for both boys' tickets. How much did she pay in all?
items.hint: Find the price of one ticket. Count one ticket for each boy.
items.explain: She paid $18. The Youth ticket row says $9, and two tickets cost $9 + $9 = $18.

items.prompt: Which food gives Clover the vitamin C she needs?
options: A small piece of red pepper
items.hint: Find the row named Vitamin C. Read it to the end.
items.explain: A small piece of red pepper. The Vitamin C row says guinea pigs cannot make their own vitamin C, so they need red pepper each day.

items.prompt: Ben has some foods in his lunch bag. Sort them for Clover.
items.hint: Read the Do not feed row. Then check the rows about hay and vitamin C.
items.explain: Red pepper and fresh hay are OK. Chocolate, potato chips and onion are in the Do not feed row.

items.prompt: It is December 3. Maya finds an old bag of these pellets in the cupboard. What should she do?
options: Ask the teacher, because the date has passed.
Give Clover twice as many pellets.
items.hint: Find the date on the bag. Is December 3 before or after it?
items.explain: Maya should ask the teacher. The Best before row says December 1, and December 3 is after that date.

items.prompt: Sam opens a pack on Monday. He eats one serving each day and closes the bag tight each time. What does the label say about his plan?
options: It works. He can take until June 30 to finish it.
It does not work. He must eat the whole pack on Monday.
It works. He finishes the pack on Wednesday, inside 5 days.
It does not work. 3 days is longer than the label allows.
items.hint: Count the servings to find the day he finishes. Then read the After opening row. Think about which date is for a closed pack.
items.explain: His plan works. The pack has 3 servings, so he finishes on Wednesday, and the After opening row says to eat it within 5 days. June 30 is the best-before date for a closed pack, so it does not count once the bag is open.

items.prompt: Sam's mom asks if any sugar was added to these strawberries. Tap the row that answers her.
items.hint: Look for a row with the word sugars in it.
items.explain: Tap the Added sugars row. It says 0 g, so no sugar was added. The Ingredients row also lists only strawberries.

items.prompt: Sam has $10. He wants as many packs as he can get. How many packs can he buy?
items.hint: Read the whole Price row. It shows two ways to buy.
items.explain: Sam can buy 3 packs. The Price row says 3 packs for $10. At $4 a pack, $10 would buy only 2 packs.

items.prompt: After the beach, Sam wants to ride on to North Bluff. What does he need to do?
options: Nothing. The day ticket covers every stop.
Buy an extra zone ticket for $2 before he gets on the train.
Buy a new day ticket for $7.
Pay $2 to the conductor after he gets on.
items.hint: Find which zone North Bluff is in. Then check the zones on his ticket.
items.explain: Sam needs an extra zone ticket for $2 before he boards. North Bluff is in Zone 4, and his ticket covers only Zones 1, 2 and 3. The North Bluff row says to buy it before you board.

items.prompt: Sam has his bike with him at Sandy Cove. Tap a train home that he can take with the bike.
items.hint: Read the Bikes row. Check each train time against it.
items.explain: Sam can take the 3:30 PM train. The Bikes row says bikes cannot go on trains that leave between 4:00 PM and 6:00 PM, and the other three trains leave inside that time.

items.prompt: Sort each plan. Does Sam's ticket cover it?

cards.text: Ride to Sandy Cove at 9:30 AM on Saturday
Ride to Sandy Cove a second time on Saturday afternoon
Ride home from Sandy Cove at 7:00 PM on Saturday
Ride to Sandy Cove at 8:30 AM on Saturday
Ride to Sandy Cove on Sunday
Ride to North Bluff with no extra ticket

items.hint: Check each plan against four rows: the day, the times, the number of trips and the zones.
items.explain: The 9:30 AM ride, a second ride and the 7:00 PM ride home are covered, because the ticket is good on Saturday from 9:00 AM to midnight for as many trips as you like. 8:30 AM is too early, Sunday is the wrong day, and North Bluff is in Zone 4.

items.prompt: The power is off. Leo wants to listen to the radio for 30 minutes. About how long should he turn the crank?
items.hint: Find how much radio time 1 minute of turning gives. Count up until you reach 30 minutes.
items.explain: About 3 minutes. The Hand crank row says 1 minute of turning gives about 10 minutes of radio, so 3 minutes gives about 30 minutes.

items.prompt: The power is off, and the family has no AA batteries. Which plan runs the radio right now?
options: Plug the USB cable into the wall outlet.
Turn the hand crank to charge the built-in battery.
Put 3 AA batteries in the radio.
Switch on the flashlight to charge the radio.
items.hint: Read both power choices. Then think about which one works with no power from the wall and no AA batteries.
items.explain: Turning the hand crank works. Power choice 2 says the crank charges the built-in battery. The wall outlet has no power, the family has no AA batteries, and the flashlight does not charge the radio.

items.prompt: Leo starts charging the radio with the USB cable at 1:00 PM. When will it be full, and how long can it play then?
options: About 5:00 PM, and it plays for about 4 hours
About 9:00 PM, and it plays for about 4 hours
About 5:00 PM, and it plays for about 8 hours
About 9:00 PM, and it plays for about 8 hours
items.hint: The USB charge row has two numbers. One is the time to charge, and one is the time it plays.
items.explain: It is full at about 5:00 PM and plays for about 8 hours. The USB charge row says full in about 4 hours, and 4 hours after 1:00 PM is 5:00 PM. A full charge plays for about 8 hours.

items.prompt: Sam runs the course in 48 minutes, but he missed 2 controls. What is his final time?
items.hint: Find the row about missed controls. Work out the extra minutes for 2 of them, then add.
items.explain: His final time is 58 minutes. The Missed a control? row adds 5 minutes for each one. 2 × 5 = 10, and 48 + 10 = 58.

items.prompt: Sam finds control 4 before he finds control 3. What should he do?
options: Leave control 4, find control 3, then come back to control 4.
Punch control 4 now, then look for control 3.
Skip both controls and go to the finish.
items.hint: Read the Controls row. Think about the order of the numbers.
items.explain: He should leave control 4, find control 3 and then come back to control 4. The Controls row says to visit the controls in number order.

items.prompt: Put Sam's race-day steps in order.
steps: Get to the start by 10:02 AM.
Hand in the card at the finish by 12:30 PM.
items.hint: Use the times on the card and the order of the controls.
items.explain: Sam gets to the start by 10:02 AM, which is 10 minutes before his 10:12 AM start. Then he punches controls 1 and 2 in number order. Last, he hands in his card by 12:30 PM.

items.prompt: The next field trip is on Saturday, May 16. What is the last day Maya can hand in her signed form?
items.hint: Find the Field trips row. Count back that many days from May 16.
items.explain: The last day is May 9. The Field trips row says at least 7 days before the trip, and 7 days before May 16 is May 9.

items.prompt: Maya brings rocks to the rock swap. Which rock is ready to trade?
options: An agate with a label: Found at Harbor Beach
A pyrite with a label: Pyrite
A quartz with a label: Quartz, found by the creek in Story Woods
items.hint: Read the Label rule row. A label needs two things. Check each rock for both.
items.explain: The quartz is ready. The Label rule row says each label needs the rock's name and the place where it was found. The pyrite label has no place, the agate label has no name, and the garnet has no label.

items.prompt: It is July 8. Maya wants to go to the club meeting next Tuesday. What does she need to do first?
options: Ask Mr. Varga about a new card, because hers was good until June 30.
Hand in a signed form 7 days before.
Nothing. Her card is still good.
items.hint: Find the date on the card. Is July 8 before or after it?
items.explain: She should ask Mr. Varga about a new card. The Card good until row says June 30, and July 8 is after that.

items.prompt: Where in his room should Sam put the plant?
options: On the windowsill, so it gets the most sun
On his desk, in bright light away from the hot sun
In his closet, where it is dark and cool
Next to the heater, so it stays warm
items.hint: Read the Light row. Then compare it with the places in Sam's room.
items.explain: On his desk. The Light row says bright light but not hot, direct sun, and the desk gets bright light without the sun shining on it. The window gets hot, direct sun.

items.prompt: On Monday, Sam touches the soil, and the top inch is still wet. What should he do?
options: Give it extra water so it lasts all week.
Wait, and check the soil again later.
Move it into the hot afternoon sun to dry.
items.hint: Read the Water row. Is the top of the soil dry yet?
items.explain: He should wait and check again later. The Water row says to water when the top inch feels dry, and too much water can rot the roots.

items.prompt: Sam worries that Pixel might chew a leaf. Tap the row that answers his worry.
items.hint: Pixel is a dog. Look for a row about animals.
items.explain: Tap the Pets row. It says the plant is safe for dogs and cats.

items.prompt: Ben goes back to the shop on October 20 with the puzzle book, still in its wrapper, and the receipt. What can he do?
options: Return it, because it is unopened and it is inside 30 days.
Only swap it for another copy of the same book.
Nothing, because he used a coupon.
Return it, but only after November 2.
items.hint: Read the Returns row. Then count the days from the date on the receipt to October 20.
items.explain: He can return it. The Returns row says unopened items can come back within 30 days with the receipt. October 20 is 17 days after October 3, and the book is still in its wrapper.

items.prompt: Without the coupon, how much would Ben's order have cost?
items.hint: Add the prices of the three things he bought. Leave out the coupon line.
items.explain: It would have cost $60.00. $40 + $12 + $8 = $60. The coupon took $10 off, so the total was $50.

items.prompt: The Galaxy Racers disc that Ben opened has a scratch, and it will not play. What does the receipt allow?
options: Return it for his money back
Swap it for a different game
Swap it for another copy of Galaxy Racers
items.hint: Read the Returns row to the end. Look for the part about opened games.
items.explain: He can swap it for another copy of Galaxy Racers. The Returns row says opened games can only be swapped for the same game.

items.prompt: How many visits are left on Ana's card?
items.hint: Find how many visits the card has. Then take away the holes that are already punched.
items.explain: 3 visits are left. The Visits row says 10, and the story says Ana's card has 7 holes. 10 - 7 = 3.

items.prompt: Ana is 12. She wants to swim at 6:30 PM on a Wednesday. What does the card say?
options: She cannot swim then. That time is lap swim for ages 13 and up.
She can swim. Open swim is on Wednesdays.
She can swim, but only in the deep end.
She can swim, because she has visits left.
items.hint: Find the row that has 6:30 PM inside its times. Then check the ages in that row.
items.explain: She cannot swim then. Open swim ends at 6:00 PM, and the Lap swim only row says 6:00 PM to 8:00 PM is for ages 13 and up. Ana is 12.

items.prompt: Ben is 12. He wants to swim in the deep end today. What must he do first?
options: Show his swim card to the lifeguard.
Pass the swim test: 2 lengths of the pool without stopping.
items.hint: Read the Deep end row. Then read the row it points to.
items.explain: He must pass the swim test first. The Deep end row says swimmers under 14 must pass it, and the Swim test row says to swim 2 lengths without stopping and to ask a lifeguard.

items.prompt: Today is November 6. Sort each food for Sam's lunch.
items.hint: Read the note first. Then check each food's date against November 6, and check if the pack is open.
items.explain: Yogurt and cheese are OK, because they are not opened and their dates are still to come. Do not eat the turkey, because its use-by date has passed, or the hummus, because it was opened 7 days ago. The crackers are past their best-before date, so Sam asks an adult first.

items.prompt: The hummus says use by November 20. Why should Sam still not eat it?
options: It has a best-before date, so he must ask an adult.
It was opened on October 30, and opened hummus must be eaten within 5 days.
items.hint: Read the last sentence of the note. Then count the days since the hummus was opened.
items.explain: It was opened on October 30, and the After opening column says to eat it within 5 days. That time ended before November 6. The note says to follow the After opening days, even if the printed date is later.

items.prompt: The crackers say best before November 2. What does the note tell Sam to do?
options: Ask an adult before he eats them.
Eat them. Best-before dates never matter.
Eat them, because the bag is open.
items.hint: Find the part of the note about BEST BEFORE.
items.explain: Sam should ask an adult before he eats them. The note says best before is about quality, and after that date you ask an adult.

items.prompt: The club buys 6 kits. How much do they pay in all?
items.hint: Check if 6 kits gets the club price. Find the price of one kit with $5 off, then count 6 of them.
items.explain: They pay $138. 6 is 5 or more, so each kit costs $28 - $5 = $23. 6 × $23 = $138.

items.prompt: The club meets once a week for 1 and a half hours. About how many meetings will Priya need to build one arm?
items.hint: Find the build time. Add 1 and a half hours for each meeting until you reach it.
items.explain: About 3 meetings. The Build time row says about 4 hours. Two meetings give only 3 hours, and three meetings give 4 and a half hours, which is enough.

items.prompt: Which of these can the robot arm lift?
options: A full water bottle that weighs 16 ounces
items.hint: Find how much the arm can lift. Compare each thing with that number. 1 pound is the same as 16 ounces.
items.explain: It can lift the 1-ounce ball. The Lifts row says up to 2 ounces. The book and the bottle each weigh 16 ounces, and the apple weighs 4 ounces.

items.prompt: On March 10, Ana wants to return the music book and the stand light. What can she return?
items.hint: Read the whole Returns row. Check the date first, then check each thing.
items.explain: Only the stand light. March 10 is before March 18, but the Returns row says music books cannot be returned.

items.prompt: Suppose Ana had bought only the music stand and the stand light. Would the coupon work?
options: Yes. The coupon works on any order.
No. The coupon is only for music books.
items.hint: Add the two prices. Then compare the total with the amount in the Coupon row.
items.explain: No. $18 + $9 = $27, and the Coupon row says the coupon works on orders of $30 or more.

items.prompt: Ms. Gray asked Ana to buy something that keeps her trumpet valves moving smoothly. Tap the row that shows she bought it.
items.hint: Look for a row that names a part of a trumpet.
items.explain: Tap the Valve oil row. Valve oil keeps trumpet valves moving smoothly, and it cost $6.00.

items.prompt: Which two dinosaurs on the box lived at the same time?
options: Each one lived at a different time.
items.hint: Read the three dinosaur rows. Look for two rows with the same numbers.
items.explain: T. rex and Triceratops. Both rows say about 68 to 66 million years ago. Stegosaurus lived about 155 to 150 million years ago, long before them.

items.prompt: About how many million years passed from the end of the Stegosaurus dates to the start of the T. rex dates?
items.hint: Find the number where Stegosaurus ends and the number where T. rex starts. Take the smaller number from the bigger one.
items.explain: About 82 million years. The Stegosaurus row ends at 150 million years ago, and the T. rex row starts at 68 million years ago. 150 - 68 = 82.

items.prompt: Sam cooks 2 servings, one for him and one for his cousin. How much dry pasta does he use, and how many servings are left in the box?
options: 1/2 cup dry, and 7 servings are left
1 cup dry, and 6 servings are left
2 cups dry, and 6 servings are left
1 cup dry, and 8 servings are left
items.hint: Find how much dry pasta is in one serving and count 2 servings. Then take 2 from the servings in the box.
items.explain: He uses 1 cup of dry pasta, and 6 servings are left. One serving is 1/2 cup dry, so 2 servings are 1 cup. The box has 8 servings, and 8 - 2 = 6.

items.prompt: Which telescope gathers more light, and why?
options: StarHopper 60, because it has more magnification
SkyView 80, because its lens is wider
items.hint: Dr. Hale said what makes a telescope gather more light. Find that line on the boxes.
items.explain: The SkyView 80 gathers more light. Dr. Hale said a wider lens gathers more light, and the Lens width row shows 80 mm, which is wider than 60 mm.

items.prompt: On Saturday, can Priya and Sam buy the SkyView 80 with their $95?
options: Yes. It costs $70, so they have $25 left.
Yes. On sale it costs $90, so they have $5 left.
items.hint: Find the price and the sale for the SkyView 80. Check if Saturday is inside the sale.
items.explain: Yes. The Sale row says $20 off until Sunday, so on Saturday the SkyView 80 costs $110 - $20 = $90. They have $95, so $5 is left.

items.prompt: They wait until Monday, and the sale is over. Which plan lets them buy a telescope that day with their $95?
items.hint: Find each telescope's price once the sale is over. Compare each price with $95.
items.explain: They can buy the StarHopper 60 for $70. After Sunday, the SkyView 80 costs the full $110, which is more than $95. The StarHopper 60 never had a sale, so it is still $70.

items.prompt: Sam and Leo go to the island and back on the same day. How much do their two tickets, Pixel's ticket and the bike cost together? Leave out Grandma Rose.
items.hint: Use the Round trip column. Add two youth tickets, one dog and one bike.
items.explain: They cost $22. Two youth round trips are $6 + $6 = $12. Pixel's round trip is $4, and the bike's round trip is $6. $12 + $4 + $6 = $22.

items.prompt: Ana and Ben's parents take the twins and their 7-year-old cousin to the island and back on the same day. What should they buy?
options: The family pass. It costs $28 instead of $30.
Single tickets. They cost $28 in all.
The family pass. It costs $28 instead of $42.
Single tickets. The cousin rides free.
items.hint: Add the round-trip tickets for 2 adults and 3 youths. Then compare that total with the family pass.
items.explain: They should buy the family pass. Single round trips cost 2 × $12 + 3 × $6 = $24 + $18 = $42, and the family pass is $28. The cousin is 7, so the cousin pays the youth fare, not the free child fare.

items.prompt: Mr. Hill goes to the island on Friday and comes back on Sunday. What should he buy?
options: Two one-way adult tickets at the dock window, $14 in all
items.hint: Read the note about round trips. Does Mr. Hill come back on the same day?
items.explain: He should buy two one-way adult tickets at the dock window, for $7 + $7 = $14. The note says a round trip is there and back on the same day, and Mr. Hill comes back two days later.

items.prompt: Maya and her dad visit 4 times this year, and they drive and park each time. Which costs less, and by how much?
items.hint: Work out one visit with day tickets and parking. Count 4 visits. Then compare with the pair membership.
items.explain: The pair membership costs $26 less. One visit with day tickets is $15 + $9 + $5 for parking = $29, so 4 visits cost $116. The pair membership is $90, and parking is free for members. $116 - $90 = $26.

items.prompt: With the membership, Maya buys a $20 sketchbook at the gift shop. How much does she pay?
items.hint: Find the gift shop discount. Work out 10% of $20, then take it off.
items.explain: Maya pays $18. The Members get row says 10% off at the gift shop, and 10% of $20 is $2. $20 - $2 = $18.

items.prompt: Maya and her dad have the pair membership. Sam comes with them one day. What does Sam need?
options: Nothing. Members' friends get in free.
items.hint: Read the Guest passes row to the end. Check which membership Maya and her dad have.
items.explain: Sam needs a youth day ticket for $9. The Guest passes row says free guest passes come with a family membership only, and Maya and her dad have the pair membership.

items.prompt: Which cereal costs the least for each ounce?
options: Honey Hoops and Oat Clouds cost the same.
items.hint: Use the Unit price row, not the Price row.
items.explain: Bran Stars costs the least for each ounce, at 25 cents. Oat Clouds is 30 cents an ounce, and Honey Hoops is 35 cents an ounce.

items.prompt: Use the note. Which cereal is high in fiber and also low in added sugars?
items.hint: Find the cereals with fiber of 20% or more. Then check which of those has added sugars of 5% or less.
items.explain: Oat Clouds. Its fiber is 21%, which is high, and its added sugars are 4%, which is low. Bran Stars is high in fiber too, but its added sugars are 18%, which is not low.

items.prompt: Ben needs 40 ounces of a cereal that is safe for Ana. He wants the safe one that costs the least per ounce. What does he buy?
items.hint: First cross out any cereal that is not safe for Ana. Then compare unit prices, and count boxes to reach 40 ounces.
items.explain: He buys 2 boxes of Oat Clouds for $12. Bran Stars may contain tree nuts, so it is not safe for Ana. Of the two safe cereals, Oat Clouds costs less per ounce: 30 cents, not 35 cents. Two 20-ounce boxes make 40 ounces, and 2 × $6 = $12.

items.prompt: Leo has $20 to put on a card. Which choice gives him the most credits?
options: Load $20 at one time, for 100 credits.
items.hint: Work out the credits for loading $10 two times. Compare that with loading $20 one time.
items.explain: Loading $20 at one time gives the most: 100 credits. Loading $10 two times gives only 40 + 40 = 80 credits.

items.prompt: Leo loads $20. He plays racing games 5 times. Then he plays 2 games of air hockey with Ben, and Leo pays for both games. How many credits are left?
items.hint: Start with the credits for $20. Take away 5 racing plays, then 2 air hockey games.
items.explain: 40 credits are left. $20 gives 100 credits. 5 racing plays use 5 × 8 = 40 credits, and 2 air hockey games use 2 × 10 = 20 credits. 100 - 40 - 20 = 40.

items.prompt: At closing time, Ben has 12 credits and 30 tickets on his card. The prize he wants costs 50 tickets. What is his best plan?
options: Keep the card, and use the credits and tickets on his next visit.
Spend the 12 credits fast, before they are gone at closing time.
Throw the card away, because 30 tickets are not enough.
Trade the 12 credits for 12 tickets at the prize counter.
items.hint: Read the Credits and tickets row. Do they disappear when the game room closes?
items.explain: He should keep the card for his next visit. The Credits and tickets row says they do not expire, so he can win more tickets later and trade them at the prize counter.

items.prompt: Sam buys the world map poster and the island rail map poster. What do they cost together this week?
items.hint: Both are posters. Read the Sale row, then halve each price before you add.
items.explain: They cost $13.50. Posters are half price this week, so the world map poster is $7.50 and the rail map poster is $6. $7.50 + $6 = $13.50. The coupon does not work, because $13.50 is less than $25.

items.prompt: Sam buys the globe, the world map poster and a pack of map pins. What is his total, and is his $30 enough?
items.hint: Find the sale prices first and add them. Then check if the coupon works, and take it off.
items.explain: His total is $30.50, so he needs 50 cents more. The poster is half price, $7.50. $25 + $7.50 + $3 = $35.50, which is $25 or more, so the coupon takes off $5. $35.50 - $5 = $30.50.

items.prompt: Use this week's sale prices. Sort each order. Does the coupon work?

cards.text: The globe and a street map
The globe and a pack of map pins
The world map poster and the rail map poster
Two world map posters and a hiking map
A hiking map, a street map and a pack of map pins

items.hint: For each order, use the sale price for any poster. Add the prices, then compare the total with $25.
items.explain: The coupon works for the globe ($25), the globe and a street map ($29), and the globe and map pins ($28). The two posters cost only $13.50 at sale prices, two world map posters and a hiking map cost $21, and the hiking map, street map and pins cost $13. Those totals are less than $25.

items.prompt: Maya starts step 1 on March 6. She starts each new step on the day the last one ends. On what day will her stones be done?
items.hint: Add up the days for all 4 steps. Then count that many days on from March 6. March has 31 days.
items.explain: Her stones will be done on April 3. Each of the 4 steps takes 7 days, so all of them take 28 days, and 28 days after March 6 is April 3.

items.prompt: Put Maya's first jobs with the tumbler in order.
steps: Have an adult help set up the tumbler.
Tumble the rocks with coarse grit for 7 days.
Rinse the rocks and the barrel well.
Tumble the rocks with medium grit for 7 days.
items.hint: The Ages row tells the first job. Then follow the step numbers, and check what happens between steps.
items.explain: First an adult helps set up the tumbler. Then come 7 days of coarse grit. Between steps, Maya rinses the rocks and the barrel. Then come 7 days of medium grit.

items.prompt: Step 1 is done, and the barrel is full of muddy grit water. What should Maya do with it?
options: Leave it in the barrel and add the medium grit.
Pour it down the kitchen sink.
Pour it into a bag and put it in the trash.
Pour it down the sink with lots of clean water.
items.hint: Read the Used grit water row. Then read the Between steps row.
items.explain: She pours it into a bag and puts it in the trash. The Used grit water row says it can block sink pipes, and the Between steps row says to rinse well, so old grit must not stay in the barrel.

items.prompt: Which station measures what the class wants, with a sensor that reaches the garden post?
options: SkyCheck Basic: it measures rainfall and wind.
SkyCheck Basic: it reaches 100 feet, which is far enough.
SkyCheck Plus: it updates every 5 minutes.
SkyCheck Plus: it measures rainfall and wind, and it reaches 300 feet.
items.hint: Check two things for each station: what it measures, and how far its sensor reaches. The post is 150 feet away.
items.explain: The SkyCheck Plus. The Measures row shows it measures rainfall and wind speed, and the Sensor range row says up to 300 feet. The Basic measures only temperature and humidity, and it reaches only 100 feet, which is less than 150 feet.

items.prompt: Ms. Ortiz orders the SkyCheck Plus on Thursday. The display will use the wall plug. How much of her $70 is left?
items.hint: Find the sale price on Thursday. Then check if she must buy any batteries.
items.explain: $5 is left. On Thursday the Plus costs $80 - $15 = $65. The display uses the wall plug, and the sensor has a solar panel with a backup battery included, so she buys no batteries. $70 - $65 = $5.

items.prompt: Sort each feature. Does only the Plus have it, or do both stations have it?

cards.text: Sensor runs on a solar panel
Display can run on 2 AA batteries

items.hint: Read across the Measures, Display power and Sensor power rows. Check both columns for each card.
items.explain: Only the Plus measures rainfall and wind speed and has a solar panel. Both stations measure temperature and humidity, and both displays can run on 2 AA batteries.

items.prompt: The family goes on Friday and Sunday only. Which passes cost the least for the three of them?
options: One-day passes on both days, $40 in all
One-day passes on both days, $80 in all
items.hint: Work out one-day passes for 1 adult and 2 youths, for 2 days. Then work out three-day passes for the same 3 people. Compare.
items.explain: One-day passes on both days cost the least, $80 in all. Each day costs $20 + $10 + $10 = $40, so 2 days cost $80. Three-day passes cost $45 + $20 + $20 = $85.

items.prompt: Suppose Ben had a three-day pass. On Friday night, his wristband feels itchy, and he wants to cut it off. He still wants to go on Sunday. What does the flyer tell him?
options: Cut it off, but keep the pieces to show at the gate.
Cut it off, and get a new one on Sunday.
Cut it off, because wristbands are for Friday only.
Keep it on, because a cut wristband is not valid.
items.hint: Find the Wristbands row. Read both sentences.
items.explain: He should keep it on. The Wristbands row says to wear it all weekend, and a cut wristband is not valid.

items.prompt: It rains on Sunday afternoon. Where and when can the family hear the piano show?
options: In the Nature Center hall at 2:00 PM
In the meadow at 2:00 PM, under umbrellas
In the Nature Center hall at 6:30 PM
items.hint: Find the time of the piano show. Then read the Rain plan row.
items.explain: In the Story Woods Nature Center hall at 2:00 PM. The Sunday row says the piano show is at 2:00 PM, and the Rain plan row says shows move into the hall at the same times.

items.prompt: Which choice lets Priya's rover drive for 2 hours without a battery change?
options: Her old ZipCell pack, fully charged
items.hint: Compare each run time with 2 hours. Remember the challenge rule about battery changes.
items.explain: One ZipCell 4000. It runs about 2 hours 30 minutes, which is more than 2 hours. One ZipCell 2000 runs only about 1 hour 15 minutes, and swapping packs is a battery change, which the challenge does not allow.

items.prompt: Priya starts charging an empty ZipCell 4000 at 7:00 PM. At 8:30 PM, she starts charging the club's empty ZipCell 2000 on a second charger. Which pack is full first, and at what time?
items.hint: Add each pack's charge time to the time it started. Then compare the two end times.
items.explain: The ZipCell 2000 is full first, at 10:30 PM. It charges in about 2 hours from 8:30 PM. The ZipCell 4000 charges in about 4 hours from 7:00 PM, so it is full at 11:00 PM.

items.prompt: After the challenge, Priya will not use her rover for six weeks. What should she do with her ZipCell 4000?
options: Charge it to about half with a phone charger, then store it.
Charge it all the way to full, then store it.
Let it run until it is empty, then store it.
Charge it to about half with the ZipCell charger, then store it.
items.hint: Read the row about storing. Then check the Charger row to see which charger to use.
items.explain: She should charge it to about half with the ZipCell charger, then store it. The Storing row says to charge it to about half for a month or more, and the Charger row says to use the ZipCell USB-C charger only.

items.prompt: Ben's mom leaves home at 5:40 PM. The drive takes 25 minutes. When will they get there, and which door should they use?
options: At 6:05 PM, at the Side Door
At 6:05 PM, at the front doors
At 6:35 PM, at the Side Door
At 6:15 PM, at the front doors
items.hint: Add 25 minutes to 5:40 PM. Then read the whole Check-in row.
items.explain: They get there at 6:05 PM and use the Side Door. 25 minutes after 5:40 PM is 6:05 PM, which is inside the check-in time, and the Check-in row says the front doors are locked after 5:00 PM.

items.prompt: Sort what Sam packs for the sleepover.
items.hint: Check each thing against the Bring row and the Do not bring row.
items.explain: Sam brings the sleeping bag, flashlight, toothbrush and pillow, which are in the Bring row. He leaves the chips and the flash camera at home, because the Do not bring row says no food and no cameras with a flash.

items.prompt: Sam's dad cannot come until 9:00 AM on Saturday. Which plan follows the pass?
options: Sam's dad comes at 7:30 AM, before breakfast.
Sam's dad comes at 9:00 AM, and the boys wait inside.
Ask Ben's mom to pick up both boys between 8:00 AM and 8:30 AM.
The boys wait at the front doors until 9:00 AM.
items.hint: Read the Pick-up row. Find the plan that fits inside those times and uses the right door.
items.explain: Ask Ben's mom to pick up both boys between 8:00 AM and 8:30 AM. The Pick-up row says pick-up is 8:00 AM to 8:30 AM at the Side Door, so 9:00 AM is too late and 7:30 AM is too early.

steps.say: I read the question first. Ana cannot eat nuts. So I need to check the label for nuts.
I look for the row that says what is in the bar. It is the Contains row.
The Contains row says oats, honey and peanuts. Peanuts are nuts.
The warning at the top says it too: Contains peanuts.
So Ana should skip this oat bar.
